import { build } from 'esbuild';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
const file = process.argv[2] ?? 'src/module.ts';
const r = await build({ entryPoints: [file], bundle: true, minify: true, treeShaking: true,
  format: 'esm', platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', write: false, metafile: true, logLevel: 'silent' });
const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)
  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

content.text:
I migrated the file to `out/module.ts`, and it imports only from es-toolkit, with no lodash import left.

- **`doubled`**: `mapValues` from es-toolkit replaces lodash's `mapValues`.
- **`byNameKey`**: es-toolkit's `keyBy` takes a function rather than a property string, so the adapter is `(row) => row.name`. On duplicate names the last row wins, the same as the original.
- **`dedupeSorted`**: es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`, so I used `uniq`. For an ascending integer array it returns the same result, since equal values are always adjacent.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 242 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of that being my own code. Type checking reports no errors for `out/module.ts`; the only errors it prints come from `src/module.ts`.

I couldn't compare against the original's size or run its outputs. `lodash` isn't in `node_modules`, so the original doesn't build or type-check. I didn't run the example inputs, so the equivalence above rests on how the functions behave, not on a test.

I tried only the root `es-toolkit` import. I didn't test other import paths, such as per-function imports, to see whether any gives a smaller bundle.
